About the role Equals Money is a fast-growing, regulated payments business on a mission to make money movement simple. As Head of Management Accounting you own the group's month-end and year-end close and the management accounts published from it — timetable, quality and team — plus the transactional finance engine that feeds the ledger (Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable and Payroll) and the controls around it. This is the role the rest of Finance depends on: FP&A, the Head of Financial Reporting and the Board rely on the management accounts closing accurately and on time. You will lead a team to deliver that every month while shortening the close and strengthening controls. Because AP, AR and Payroll sit in your team, you own data quality where it enters the ledger, not only when it's reported. Reporting to the Group Finance Director, this is a mid-senior leadership role for a qualified accountant who takes pride in a clean, well-controlled close and in transactional processes that pay suppliers, customers and colleagues correctly. Responsibilities Month-End Close Own the group month-end close end-to-end: set the timetable and hold the team and business to working day 3 (draft) and working day 5 (published), every month without exception; detail may be refined afterwards, but published numbers do not change. Design, build and publish a quality-assured management accounts pack for the group and each entity — P&L, balance sheet and cashflow against budget, forecast and prior year, with commentary on every material variance — plus a granular P&L to every cost centre owner. Work with FP&A and the Head of Finance Projects to load budgets and forecasts into the ledger, including the roll-up structure to compare actuals to higher-level budgets; reconcile and challenge accruals, prepayments, provisions and intercompany allocations before release. Own the balance sheet — every account reconciled, reviewed and substantiated, ageing items cleared — and provide variance analysis that gives FP&A a reliable platform for insight. Maintain the general ledger and NetSuite to a high standard: chart of accounts integrity, the dimensions and roll-ups to report by entity, cost centre and product, clean separation of one-off items, and consistent posting discipline. Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable & Payroll Own AP, AR and Payroll as part of the team, holding each to the same standards of accuracy, timeliness and control as the close itself. AP: no PO, no payment — approval thresholds so spend is approved before it's incurred; supplier onboarding and bank detail changes verified with dual authorisation; payment runs to agreed terms, managing creditor days as a KPI; AP ledger drives accruals (GRNI, unprocessed invoices). AR: invoice accurately and immediately so revenue is billed in the period earned; a disciplined weekly collections cycle with debtor days as a KPI; credit control set at customer onboarding; expected credit loss policy applied consistently, agreed with the Head of Financial Reporting. Payroll: right pay, right day, every time — own the timetable and exception review; control starters/leavers with People; reconcile to the ledger and HMRC monthly (PAYE, NI, pensions); account for bonus, commission, holiday pay and share incentive costs with Financial Reporting; confidential by design. Report AP, AR and Payroll performance monthly — creditor and debtor days, aged debt, invoice ageing, payroll accuracy — and work with Treasury and FP&A on cash and working capital. Year-End Delivery Own the Finance function's delivery of year-end close, ensuring ledgers close accurately and to timetable, working closely with the Head of Financial Reporting on the schedules and evidence needed for statutory accounts and audit. Resolve accounting queries and audit requests promptly, pre-empting likely auditor focus areas before fieldwork, and keep management and statutory accounting treatment consistent, explaining any differences clearly. Support the Head of Financial Reporting on interim audit work in Q4, including a full set of accounts on an 8+4 forecast basis. Control & Quality Maintain and strengthen the control environment around the close — quality-assured numbers, segregation of duties, approval thresholds and a documented close checklist, operable by more than one person. Own anti-fraud controls around outbound payments and payroll, including bank detail verification, dual authorisation and prompt investigation of suspected fraud. Own the Chart of Accounts, with a named owner and regular review per account code, and ensure data released into the data warehouse is Finance-approved and reconciled to the ledger first. Support the Head of Financial Reporting and Chief Internal Auditor on financial risk assessment, control testing and remediation. Team Leadership Lead, develop and hold accountable your team — including AP, AR and Payroll — setting clear expectations on quality, timeliness and ownership, and allocate work to build resilience and cross-cover so the timetable depends on no one individual. Manage the transfer of management accounting activities into the team as they automate and move from entity finance teams, ensuring process and controls transfer cleanly, and set the tone for the team's engagement with the business — responsive, constructive and commercially aware. Continuous Improvement Systematically shorten and de-risk the close, targeting manual journals and spreadsheet dependency, working with the Head of Finance Projects on automation, and standardise treatment across entities as the group integrates. Embrace automation and agentic AI within the close — automated NetSuite feeds, reconciliation and machine-prepared first-cut reporting — and extend it into transactional finance (invoice capture, automated matching and cash allocation, payroll checking) so the team focuses on exceptions and insight rather than keying. Key relationships Day to day: the Group Finance Director, your team, the Head of Financial Reporting (year-end/audit), the Head of FP&A and Directors of Financial Control. Beyond Finance: budget holders, Finance Projects, People (payroll/reward), Commercial/Operations. Externally: suppliers, our payroll provider and customers' finance teams. Proven ownership of a multi-entity month-end close delivered to a demanding timetable, with success improving a close — shortening timetables or strengthening controls. Experience leading and developing a team; designing and launching a management reporting pack (cost centre reporting) is a strong advantage. Experience owning transactional finance (AP, AR, Payroll) — the controls, KPIs and stakeholder relationships that go with it — plus a working understanding of UK payroll obligations (PAYE, NI, pensions, benefits). Advanced Excel and confident use of an ERP general ledger; NetSuite and payments/e-money experience are advantages but not essential. Attitude & Behaviours Deadline-driven and rigorous — you treat the timetable as a commitment, reconcile properly, and never sign off on numbers you can't explain. A custodian of working capital — you treat the balance sheet and cashflow as important as the P&L, knowing how we bill, collect and pay matters as much as the profit we report. Discreet with payroll and colleague data. A capable manager who gets work done through the team, and a clear communicator to budget holders and the CFO alike. Improvement-minded and a publisher, not just a preparer — you get numbers to people who can act on them, highlighting trends and opportunities to drive revenue or cut costs. Diversity & inclusion Equals is committed to building a workplace where everyone can be themselves. We actively welcome different perspectives, backgrounds and experiences, and we'll work with you to understand what you need to do your best work. We're an equal opportunities employer and proud of it. We offer hybrid working, balancing time in the office with the flexibility to work remotely where roles allow.
